arxiv-1911-11753.title: Gravitational Collapse for the K- essence Emergent Vaidya Spacetime
arxiv-1911-11753.creator: Goutam Manna
arxiv-1911-11753.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Goutam Manna. In this paper, we study the gravitational collapse in the k- essence emergent gravity using a generalized Vaidya-type metric as a background. We also analyze the cosmic censorship hypothesis for this system. We show that the emergent gravity metric resembles closely to the new type of the generalized Vaidya metrics for null fluid collapse with the k- essence emergent mass function, where we consider the k- essence scalar field being a function solely of the advanced or the retarded time.

arxiv-2101-02650.description: Abstract We report the nanoscale spin detection and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectrum of copper (Cu 2+ ) ions via double electron-electron resonance with single spins in diamond at room temperature and low magnetic fields. We measure unexpectedly narrow EPR resonances with linewidths ∼ 2 − 3 \sim 2-3 MHz from copper-chloride molecules dissolved in poly-lysine.

arxiv-2208-02146.title: Thermo-acoustics and its detection in a premixed flame
arxiv-2208-02146.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . A new optical technique based on light-matter interaction is devised in-house to detect thermo-acoustic disturbances generated after ignition and during propagation of a premixed flame front in a half open channel. The technique involves passing a polarized laser light through a medium whose density or refractive index varies due to the passage of acoustic waves and/or flame front and then capturing the leaked depolarised light through an analyser by a photo-detector.

arxiv-2411-13760.creator: Luke Guerdan, Hanna Wallach, Solon Barocas, Alexandra Chouldechova
arxiv-2411-13760.description: Abstract Large language model (LLM) evaluations often assume there is a single correct response—a gold label —for each item in the evaluation corpus. arxiv-2505-16390.title: Observational Properties of Thermal Emission from Relativistic Jets Embedded in AGN Disks
arxiv-2505-16390.creator: Ken Chen, Zi-Gao Dai
arxiv-2505-16390.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ken Chen, Zi-Gao Dai. Relativistic jets can be produced within the accretion disk of an active galactic nucleus (AGN), leading to distinct thermal emission as they propagate through a dense disk environment. In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of dynamical evolution of jets embedded in an AGN disk and their associated observational properties, focusing on scenarios in which jets either successfully break out of the disk or become choked.

arxiv-2506-01425.title: CSVAR: Enhancing Visual Privacy in Federated Learning via Adaptive Shuffling Against Overfitting
arxiv-2506-01425.creator: Zhuo Chen, Zhenya Ma, Yan Zhang, Donghua Cai, Ye Zhang, Qiushi Li, Yongheng Deng, Ye Guo
arxiv-2506-01425.description: Abstract Although federated learning preserves training data within local privacy domains, the aggregated model parameters may still reveal private characteristics. This vulnerability stems from clients’ limited training data, which predisposes models to overfitting. Such overfitting enables models to memorize distinctive patterns from training samples, thereby amplifying the success probability of privacy attacks like membership inference.

pmc-12500154.title: Microsaccades strongly modulate but do not directly cause the EEG N2pc marker of spatial attention
pmc-12500154.creator: Baiwei Liu, Siyang Kong, Freek van Ede, Christian Schnell, PhD, Christian Schnell, PhD, Christian Schnell, PhD, Christian Schnell, PhD, Christian Schnell, PhD
pmc-12500154.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The N2pc is a popular human-neuroscience marker of covert and internal spatial attention that occurs 200–300 ms after being prompted to shift attention—a time window also characterized by the spatial biasing of small fixational eye movements known as microsaccades. Here, we show how co-occurring microsaccades profoundly modulate N2pc amplitude during top-down shifts of spatial attention in both perception and working memory. At the same time, we show that a significant—albeit severely weakened—N2pc can still be established in the absence of co-occurring microsaccades.
